content.goal: Decide, first, WHY a sub-agent is justified here.
content.why: Multi-agent is frequently overused. Before building one, you must be able to say why a single agent won't do. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 14, section 14.1.)
content.code:
# Write your justification as a comment:
#  - The RESEARCH sub-task (searching + synthesizing from docs) needs a focused
#    prompt and only the search_docs tool — isolation reduces what can go wrong.
#  - The MAIN agent orchestrates and also does word counts / reversing.
#  - Contract: research returns a short {"summary":..., "sources":[...]} object.
content.verify: You have a specific, written reason each agent exists and a defined contract between them. If you couldn't write this, you would stay single-agent.

content.goal: Build the specialist as a function that runs its OWN small loop — then expose it as a tool.
content.why: The cleanest multi-agent design: a sub-agent is just something the coordinator can CALL, exactly like a tool. Coordination stays explicit. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 14, section 14.2.)
content.code:
def research_agent(question: str) -> dict:
    """A focused sub-agent: searches the user's docs and returns a grounded summary."""
    chunks = retrieve(question, k=3)
    context = "\n\n".join(f"(source: {c['source']}) {c['text']}" for c in chunks)
    summary = ask([
        {"role": "system", "content":
         "You are a research specialist. Summarize an answer to the question using ONLY the context. "
         "Return 2-3 sentences and say if the context is insufficient."},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"Context:\n{context}\n\nQuestion: {question}"},
    ])
    return {"summary": summary, "sources": list({c["source"] for c in chunks})}

TOOL_IMPLS["research"] = research_agent
content.verify: The file saves. research_agent runs its own retrieval + reasoning and returns a STRUCTURED contract ({"summary", "sources"}) — a validated hand-off, not free-form chatter.

content.goal: Register the sub-agent as a tool on the supervisor.
content.why: To the supervisor, "research" looks like any other tool — but behind it sits a whole specialist agent. This is the supervisor (hub-and-spoke) topology, the recommended default. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 14, section 14.3.)
content.verify: The file saves. The supervisor (your run_agent) now has a "research" tool. Workers do not talk to each other — only to the supervisor.

content.goal: Run a task where the supervisor delegates to the specialist and then finishes.
content.why: This exercises hub-and-spoke delegation with a clean contract — the reliable multi-agent shape. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 14, section 14.4.)
content.verify: The trace shows the supervisor call the "research" tool (which internally searches and summarizes), receive the structured summary, then use reverse_text, then answer. Two levels of agent, coordination fully explicit.
content.troubleshoot: If the supervisor tries to research everything, sharpen the tool description ("only when reading the user's files is required"). Keep the contract structured — never free-form prose between the two.

content.goal: Add a GLOBAL step budget across supervisor and sub-agent.
content.why: Termination and cost are the hard parts of multi-agent — cap total work across ALL agents, not just per agent. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 14, section 14.5.)
content.code:
# Pass a shared budget object into both run_agent and research_agent, e.g.:
#   budget = {"steps": 0, "max": 12}
# Increment budget["steps"] on every model call in either agent; if it exceeds
# budget["max"], stop with "Stopped: global step budget exhausted."
content.verify: A task that would otherwise spiral now stops when the COMBINED work of supervisor plus specialist hits the global cap. Normal tasks finish well within it.

content.why: You built the recommended multi-agent shape with an explicit contract and a global budget.
content.verify: All true — you justified why the sub-agent exists; the specialist runs its own loop and returns a structured contract; the supervisor calls it like a tool; a global step budget bounds the whole system.
